related_questions.question: What is the best thing to take if you have COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: The best treatment for COVID-19 often involves symptom management and, for some, medications to reduce the risk of severe illness. For mild cases, over-the-counter medications like fever reducers (acetaminophen or ibuprofen) and cough suppressants can help alleviate symptoms. If you are at higher risk of severe COVID-19, your doctor might prescribe antiviral medications, like Paxlovid, Molnupiravir, or Remdesivir, which need to be started within a few days of symptom onset.
snippet_highlighted_words: over-the-counter medications like fever reducers (acetaminophen or ibuprofen) and cough suppressants

list.snippet: Rest: Getting adequate rest is crucial for recovery.
Hydration: Staying hydrated with plenty of fluids helps with recovery.
Fever reducers: Acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) can help lower fever and relieve pain.
Cough suppressants: Medications containing dextromethorphan or guaifenesin can help relieve cough.
Decongestants: If you have nasal congestion, decongestants like pseudoephedrine or phenylephrine can help, but consult with a doctor or pharmacist if you have other health conditions.

list.title: Antiviral medications:
list.snippet: If you are at higher risk of severe COVID-19, your doctor may prescribe antiviral medications like Paxlovid, Molnupiravir, or Remdesivir. These medications are most effective when started within the first few days of symptom onset.

list.title: Monoclonal antibodies:
list.snippet: In some cases, monoclonal antibodies may be an option for treatment, but these are typically administered in a healthcare setting.

list.title: Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing:
list.snippet: This is a serious symptom that requires immediate medical attention.

list.title: Persistent fever:
list.snippet: If your fever lasts for more than a few days or is very high, consult with a doctor.

list.title: Dehydration:
list.snippet: If you are unable to keep fluids down or are showing signs of dehydration, seek medical advice.

list.title: Underlying health conditions:
list.snippet: If you have underlying health conditions, it's important to consult with your doctor about the best course of treatment for COVID-19.

list.title: Symptoms worsen:
list.snippet: If your symptoms are getting worse or not improving after a few days, seek medical advice.

list.title: Consult with a doctor:
list.snippet: It's always best to consult with your doctor or other healthcare provider to determine the best course of treatment for your specific situation. They can assess your risk factors and recommend the most appropriate medications and therapies.

list.title: Follow instructions carefully:
list.snippet: If your doctor prescribes medication, be sure to follow the instructions carefully and complete the full course of treatment, even if you start feeling better.

list.title: Be aware of potential drug interactions:
list.snippet: If you are taking other medications, be sure to inform your doctor or pharmacist about them to avoid potential drug interactions.

list.title: Stay informed about current guidelines:
list.snippet: Public health recommendations regarding COVID-19 treatment may change over time, so it's important to stay informed about the latest guidelines from reputable sources like the CDC.
